# Operational protocol for the Moriarty DeFi Kernel

**Date:** 2026-09-29. **Status:** advisory architecture memo from one architect. It is not an adopted MIL/4 profile, not an implementation, and not a consensus of the study. This consultation did not re-run guarded status, did not edit product code, and did not retrieve pages beyond the source packet supplied with the question. Primary URLs already quoted in that packet are cited as packet-sourced. Five further public documents are cited from prior knowledge of those documents, not from a fresh fetch in this session.

## Recommendation

Specify the optional Federated DeFi Kernel as a **fact-append reconciliation service** with four independent rails per logical leg (control, source, effect, recovery). Derive every caller-visible phase from those facts. Freeze a second dispatch, a refund, and a cancel-success claim while any required fact is `unknown`. Treat solver quotes, threshold signatures, queue logs, inclusions, finality attestations, fills, oracle rounds, refunds, and compensations as different records.

Keep this machine in the kernel interaction profile. The permissionless intent language continues to state the signed financial relation, the settlement locus, the evidence class, and the exclusive acceptable outcomes. A direct Midnight program remains valid with no kernel in the path. The packet’s NEAR proposal already characterizes the consolidated design as placing cross-chain routing, threshold custody, finality observation, and recovery in that optional federation. This memo follows that characterization.

The single ladder `planned → … → delivered | refunded | failed | unknown` is a useful vocabulary for a receipt. It is the wrong store for retry. A writable ladder is Design A below and should be rejected as the protocol state.

## What is source-grounded, and what is inferred

**Packet facts used here.**

- NEAR’s verifier holds credited balances and can settle a signed intent in one verifier transaction. Deposit, external withdrawal, solver broadcast, and bridge routes sit outside that atomicity. Each listed bridge route has its own trust model. Chain Signatures produce a threshold signature over a caller-supplied payload; the caller broadcasts. A BTC refund path requires a nonfinal deposit, a timelock, a contract action, MPC signing, and relayer broadcast, and it charges a non-returned storage deposit. Sources: [verifier](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/verifier-contract/introduction), [market makers](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/market-makers/introduction), [bridges](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/bridging/overview), [Chain Signatures](https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/chain-signatures), [BTC refund](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/bridging/btc-deposit-refund), [intents repo](https://github.com/near/intents), [mpc repo](https://github.com/near/mpc).
- HyperCore holds order book, matching, and margin under HyperBFT. HyperEVM CoreWriter actions can be enqueued and executed later. The exchange API distinguishes resting from filled and distinguishes order, cancel, modify, withdrawal, and other actions. Builder-fee approval is a separate, revocable maximum. API-wallet nonce state is per signer, and pruning a deregistered agent can make old actions replayable if the address is reused. Oracle inputs are validator-published. The Arbitrum USDC bridge is a workflow of withdrawal request, validator signing, and external submission. Sources: [Core](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/overview), [order book](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/order-book), [CoreWriter](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/interacting-with-hypercore), [timings](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/interaction-timings), [exchange](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint), [nonces](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/nonces-and-api-wallets), [builder codes](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/builder-codes), [oracle](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/oracle), [HIP-3](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hyperliquid-improvement-proposals-hips/hip-3-builder-deployed-perpetuals).
- The Aeon bridge probe on pinned commit `ef66bd95e6b7d2d5309453ee63640bc7fa1d988f` rejected full refunds justified only by timeout, unknown status, a zero observation, or a positive partial delivery, and accepted a residual refund only when `delivered` was supplied as a premise. Details and limits are in the Aeon section.
- The same pin’s authority probe accepted an impossible gross-cap refinement and a bare `false` term. The signing probe kept abstract phase tags apart and also accepted a `native` value declared as finalized.

**Inferences.** The identifier grammar, the two machines, the freeze rule, and the trace judgments below are design proposals from those facts. They are not NEAR, Hyperliquid, Aeon, or Moriarty implementation results. Hyperliquid documentation was not cross-checked against HyperCore source or a live transaction. NEAR’s components are not one operator and do not share one security assumption.

## Further primary literature

These five are outside the packet’s NEAR and Hyperliquid pages. They were not re-fetched for this memo. Claims are limited to what that literature is reliably known to say.

1. Herlihy, Liskov, and Shrira, “Cross-chain Deals and Adversarial Commerce,” https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.09743. Independent ledgers do not share one atomic commit. A cross-chain deal escrows assets on each ledger and uses publication and time. Completing the exchange, and refunding escrow, are different admissible outcomes. A coordinator’s local timer is not a ledger fact.
2. ERC-7683, Cross Chain Intents, https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7683. The settlement interface defines an origin `open` and a destination `fill`, with swapper nonce, origin chain, initiate deadline, fill deadline, and outputs that name token, amount, recipient, and chain. The order id and the on-chain settler are the replay boundary. The solver auction is outside the interface. A deadline is an order field, not proof that the destination failed to fill.
3. IBC ICS-004 channel and packet semantics, https://github.com/cosmos/ibc/blob/main/spec/core/ics-004-channel-and-packet-semantics/README.md. A packet has a channel sequence and a source commitment. Receive, acknowledgement, and timeout are protocol steps. Timeout requires proof that the packet was not received and that the timeout height or timestamp has been met. Acknowledgement and timeout are alternatives for the same packet. An application acknowledgement can still carry an application error, which is a completed receive, not a timeout.
4. ERC-4337, https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4337. A `UserOperation` has a sender, a nonce, calldata, and a signature. The EntryPoint consumes the nonce when it accepts the operation. Validation, inclusion, and the success of the inner call are different stages. Nonce consumption can outlive an inner call that did not produce the user’s intended effect.
5. Circle CCTP contracts and documentation, https://github.com/circlefin/evm-cctp-contracts and https://developers.circle.com/cctp. Source `depositForBurn` emits a message. A Circle attestation signs that message. Destination `receiveMessage` mints and consumes the message identity so the same attestation cannot mint twice. Burn, attestation, and mint are three facts. The attestation signer is a named trust premise, not a light client of the source chain.

The HTTP Idempotency-Key draft is the same shape as the kernel’s attempt rule (same key and same fingerprint return the stored result; same key and a different fingerprint conflict). It is an API storage convention. It is not used as a sixth source and it does not bind a chain.

## Identifiers

Use one canonical hash, the same function the envelope already uses. The byte encoding remains the open M4-C5 choice. Until that choice exists, these are logical identities.

| Id | Defined over | Retries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IntentId` | Canonical signed envelope bytes | Stable for the whole workflow |
| `QuoteId` | Solver key, `IntentId`, canonical quote bytes, expiry | A new quote is a new id. A quote is not an effect |
| `PlanId` | `IntentId`, selected `QuoteId`, ordered leg commitments, adapter id and version | Same plan repeats as a no-op. A different plan conflicts while the first is held |
| `LegId` | `PlanId`, ordinal, action class, settlement locus, domain, payload commitment, recipient, venue-order key or bridge claim key | Every retry of the same logical effect reuses this id |
| `AttemptId` | `LegId` and a monotonic `attempt_ordinal` | A new ordinal is a new submission. It is legal only after reconciliation |
| `SignRequestId` | `LegId`, domain, chain id, key epoch, derivation path, scheme, payload digest, recipient, value, nonce, validity window | Same id returns the stored signature. Any field change is a different request and must not be signed under the old grant |
| `ObservationId` | Subject id, evidence class, issuer, round or transaction id, statement hash | Same id is a no-op import. A different statement for the same issuer and round is equivocation, not an overwrite |

Domain-native identifiers stay attributes of an attempt or an observation: transaction hash, venue order id, client order key, bridge message or claim or nullifier, oracle round, CoreWriter action version and log index. They never replace `LegId`. Hyperliquid’s exchange API is the kind of venue that can rest an order and later fill it; the kernel must store the venue order id once observed and must also have its own id before the venue answers. Where that venue documents a client-supplied order id, bind it to `LegId`. Where it does not, any send whose acceptance is unclear stays `broadcast_unknown` and blocks another send.

`IntentId` binds authority. `LegId` binds the logical effect. `AttemptId` binds one submission. Collapsing these three into one nonce is the duplicated-dispatch failure.

## Idempotency, retry, and reconciliation

Run this procedure before every new attempt, cancel claim, refund, compensation, or language handoff.

1. Load every `AttemptId` and `ObservationId` for the `LegId`.
2. Re-query each non-terminal attempt at its named settlement locus.
3. Append a fact only when the evidence class in the table below allows that fact.
4. Recompute cumulative delivered, cumulative refunded, open residual, and fees. Delivery is monotonic per native fill or mint id. The same fill id does not increase the cumulative. Distinct fill ids add.
5. If any attempt is `broadcast_unknown`, included below finality, effect-`unknown`, or `enqueued` without an execution observation, set control to `dispatch_frozen` and close the refund edge.
6. If one `LegId` has two native effect identities (two venue order ids, two successful claims, two mints), set recovery to `breach` and freeze.
7. Allocate a new `attempt_ordinal` only when every prior attempt is `rejected_before_effect` or `dropped_before_final` by evidence, and the payload commitment is unchanged.
8. A changed recipient, fee, domain, payload, claim id, adapter version, or key epoch is a new `LegId`. It needs a new check against the signed envelope. It is not a retry.
9. Return the rails, the cumulatives, and the evidence references. There is no success Boolean.

Per operation:

| Operation | Key | Retry and reconciliation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solver quote | `QuoteId` | Repeatable read. Expiry makes it unusable. A quote may refine caps, recipient, fee, and failure policy. It cannot widen them. Selection writes one `PlanId`. Quote performance is an operational promise, not settlement |
| Plan reserve | (`IntentId`, `PlanId`) | Kernel-local. Expiry releases it with no chain action. Reservation does not consume financial authority |
| `validatePlan` | `PlanId` | Pure recompute against the envelope, the pinned adapter, and the evidence profile. Required before any `SignRequest` or external submission |
| Signer call | `SignRequestId` | Sign only a payload produced by the pinned adapter for that leg. Store the signature. A second identical request returns it. A substituted digest, path, chain, recipient, value, epoch, or nonce is refused. Signing establishes key participation over those bytes |
| Native venue order | `LegId` plus venue order id once known | Resting is an open duty. Partial fills append. Modify and cancel are new attempts that reference the same venue order. A second full order is a second effect |
| CoreWriter-like queue | `AttemptId` for the EVM send; action id inside the log for execution | The enqueue log and the later core execution are separate observations. A second EVM send is forbidden while the first is unknown, included, or enqueued. If the core action has no venue-enforced unique id, two included enqueues can both execute; the adapter then has no safe automatic retry |
| Bridge leg | `LegId` bound to the route’s claim, message, or nullifier | Track source lock or burn, relay, destination credit, and source refund as separate facts. Cumulative destination credit plus source refund stays within the authorized entitlement |
| Oracle import | `ObservationId` including issuer and round | Re-import is a no-op. A new round is a new observation. The kernel does not relabel a round as verified and does not average issuers. A bond or a slash is not a price |
| Finality | Named policy on that leg | Policies are venue-consensus, inclusion depth, light client, and named quorum. One policy’s evidence does not satisfy another. Signature-only enforcement must be written in the grant, because quorum compromise then bypasses the Moriarty check |
| Cancellation | Cancel `AttemptId` plus the observed native id | The request and the dead-order fact are separate. Cumulative fills stay. With no observed native id and a source still unknown, cancel cannot be treated as effective |
| Compensation | New `LegId`, parent pointer, new authority check | A new payment or transfer. It does not delete, reverse, or rewrite the parent facts. Gross lifetime caps still apply |
| Recovery | Derived from the rails | From `unknown`, the legal acts are observe, reconcile, and manual escalate. Escalation does not create a non-execution fact |

Settlement locus is mandatory on every leg: Midnight verifier, foreign venue ledger, same-chain system contract, bridge source, or bridge destination. Only that locus’s verifier can establish that leg’s fact. This split is the packet’s architectural inference from Hyperliquid’s native core versus its external bridge, and it matches NEAR’s split between verifier atomicity and external bridges.

## Evidence classes

| Class | Example | What it may advance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E0 | Kernel log of a plan or reservation | Control rail only |
| E1 | Solver-signed quote | Reservation, after it refines the envelope |
| E2 | User envelope signature | Authority check. Assumed, not re-proved, by the Aeon probes |
| E3 | Agent or threshold signature | Source rail to `signed` |
| E4 | Transport acknowledgement that names the payload hash | Source rail to `broadcast_unknown` |
| E5 | Inclusion or queue log naming the committed bytes | Source to `included`, or effect to `enqueued` |
| E6 | Finality under the named policy | Source, destination, or refund finality for that domain only |
| E7 | Fill, mint, credit, or core execution, with an amount and a native id | Effect cumulative |
| E8 | Proof of non-execution or of no further delivery: IBC-style non-receipt, consumed nullifier plus a final remainder, or a venue order that is dead at a stated cumulative | `unavailable_proven`, or final-exclusive on a partial cumulative |
| E9 | Operator or host report | Only what a signed policy names that issuer to attest. It does not upgrade to E6, E7, or E8 |

A timeout, an empty observation, and the status code `unknown` are E0 clock or gap records. They are not E8.

## Design A — coupled ladder

One state per leg:

`planned`, `reserved`, `authorized`, `signed`, `submitted`, `included`, `finalized`, `delivered`, `cancel_requested`, `refunding`, `refunded`, `compensating`, `failed`, `unknown`.

| From | To | Evidence that would be required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `planned` | `reserved` | E1 quote still inside the E2 caps; E0 reservation |
| `reserved` | `authorized` | `validatePlan` against pinned adapter and payload commitment |
| `authorized` | `signed` | E3 for that `SignRequestId` |
| `signed` | `submitted` | E4 |
| `submitted` | `included` | E5 |
| `included` | `finalized` | E6 |
| `finalized` | `delivered` | E7 |
| any non-terminal | `unknown` | Loss of observation, conflict, or timer |
| `unknown` | a prior state | Only a positive E5, E6, or E7 for that exact state |
| `finalized` | `refunding` | E8 non-delivery, or a final E7 cumulative with refund amount ≤ remainder |
| `refunding` | `refunded` | E6 and E7 on the refund domain |
| `delivered` or `refunded` | `compensating` | A new authorized leg; the prior state would have to remain |

**Where this machine breaks.** One cell cannot represent source-final and destination-unknown together, a resting order, a partial fill, an enqueued CoreWriter action, or two attempts. The natural implementation writes `unknown` on a timer and then takes `unknown → refunding` from the timer. That is the transition the Aeon bridge probe rejected. Late destination success has nowhere to land once the cell says `refunding`. A duplicate send overwrites `submitted` instead of recording a second native order. Design A may be projected for display. It must not be the store.

A saga variant of Design A, which emits an automatic compensating transaction on timeout, fails the same way. Compensation is not an inverse mint, and ICS-004-style timeout is legal only with a non-receipt proof.

## Design B — four rails

Recommended machine. Each `LegId` has a set of attempt records plus these rails.

**Control:** `idle`, `reserved`, `dispatch_allowed`, `dispatch_frozen`, `recovery_allowed`, `closed`.

**Source, per `AttemptId`:** `none`, `signed`, `broadcast_unknown`, `included`, `final`, `rejected_before_effect`, `dropped_before_final`.

**Effect, per logical claim or venue order:** `none`, `enqueued`, `open_residual`, `partial`, `full`, `unavailable_proven`, `unknown`.

**Recovery:** `none`, `cancel_requested`, `cancel_effective`, `refund_requested`, `refund_final`, `compensation_open`, `compensation_final`, `breach`.

Derived outcome, recomputed, never written by an operator:

| Derived | Rails that produce it |
| --- | --- |
| `open` | Residual duty remains, recovery is not `breach`, no required fact is `unknown` |
| `succeeded` | Effect `full`, recovery has no refund and no breach, no attempt is unknown |
| `closed_accounted` | Cumulative delivered plus cumulative refunded equals the accounted entitlement, remainder is final-exclusive under E8, no attempt is unknown, recovery is not `breach` |
| `failed_clean` | Every attempt is `rejected_before_effect` or `dropped_before_final`, effect is `unavailable_proven`, delivered and refunded are zero |
| `unknown` | Any required source or effect fact is `unknown` or `enqueued` or `broadcast_unknown`, and recovery is not `breach` |
| `breach` | Delivered plus refunded exceeds entitlement, two native effect ids exist for one `LegId`, or a refund finalized while a conflicting delivery also finalized |

`breach` is sticky. Later evidence can add to the cumulatives. It cannot clear the flag.

### Transitions Design B allows

Source rail, each attempt:

| From | To | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | `signed` | E3 matching `SignRequestId` |
| `signed` | `broadcast_unknown` | E4, or a local send record with no authenticated acceptance |
| `broadcast_unknown` | `included` | E5 naming that payload |
| `broadcast_unknown` | `rejected_before_effect` | Authenticated venue or chain rejection that establishes no effect was created |
| `broadcast_unknown` | `dropped_before_final` | E8 that this payload is absent from the canonical chain after its validity window and that no effect exists |
| `included` | `final` | E6 for this locus |
| `included` | `dropped_before_final` | Reorg evidence below the finality policy, and no E7 for this attempt |
| `final` | `final` | Sticky for this attempt |

Effect rail:

| From | To | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | `enqueued` | E5 CoreWriter-style log with action version and committed bytes |
| `enqueued` | `open_residual`, `partial`, or `full` | E7 core execution or venue result for that action id |
| `none` | `open_residual` | E7 resting order, amount still open |
| `open_residual` | `partial` | E7 cumulative `0 < q < committed` |
| `partial` | `partial` | E7 strictly greater cumulative, new native fill id |
| `open_residual` or `partial` | `full` | E7 cumulative meets the committed amount |
| `none` or `unknown` | `unavailable_proven` | E8 |
| `none` | `unknown` | Gap, timer, or conflicting E9 with no E7 |
| `unknown` | `partial`, `full`, or `unavailable_proven` | A new E7 or E8. The timer is not that evidence |
| `full` | `full` | Sticky. A later smaller report is a stale observation |

A partial cumulative becomes final-exclusive only with an additional E8 that no further delivery can occur for that claim. Until then the refund edge stays closed. This is the operational form of the Aeon result that `refund = sent - delivered` is sound only when `delivered` is the complete figure.

Recovery rail:

| From | To | Evidence and guard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | `cancel_requested` | Authorized cancel attempt dispatched |
| `cancel_requested` | `cancel_effective` | E7 or E8 that the native order or claim is dead. The effect cumulative is unchanged by this edge |
| `none` | `refund_requested` | Source is `final` or `rejected_before_effect`; effect is `unavailable_proven` or `partial` with final-exclusive E8; refund amount ≤ entitlement − delivered − already refunded; no attempt is `unknown`, `broadcast_unknown`, or `enqueued` |
| `refund_requested` | `refund_final` | E6 and E7 on the refund domain |
| `refund_requested` | `none` | Refund aborted with evidence, before refund finality, because destination delivery moved |
| `none` | `compensation_open` | New `LegId` authorized against the parent breach or shortfall |
| `compensation_open` | `compensation_final` | That new leg reached `succeeded` or `closed_accounted` |
| any | `breach` | Invariant failure above. Parent facts remain |

Control:

| To | When |
| --- | --- |
| `reserved` | E0 plan held, no attempt sent |
| `dispatch_allowed` | `validatePlan` passed, no attempt is in flight, payload still matches |
| `dispatch_frozen` | Any unknown, included-unfinal, enqueue-without-execution, or second native effect id |
| `recovery_allowed` | A recovery-row guard holds |
| `closed` | Derived outcome is `succeeded`, `closed_accounted`, `failed_clean`, or `breach` and any required compensation leg is itself accounted |

Oracle observations do not move these rails by themselves. A leg whose policy names an oracle round may enter `dispatch_allowed` only while that `ObservationId` matches issuer, round, and freshness. A later round governs later legs. It does not rewrite a fill that already has E7.

## Positive traces

**P1. Two quotes, one native order, later full fill.** The envelope fixes recipient, domain, gross cap, and fee cap (E2). Solver A quotes inside the fee cap. Solver B quotes a larger fee. `validatePlan` rejects B and reserves A (E1, E0). The plan pins the adapter version and payload commitment. The signer call matches `SignRequestId` and the source rail becomes `signed` (E3). Attempt 1 is dispatched with the client order key bound to `LegId`. The venue reports the order resting, so the effect rail becomes `open_residual` (E7 under the issuer the policy names for that API). A later observation brings the cumulative to the committed amount under the venue finality policy (E7, E6). Derived outcome: `succeeded`. No refund leg exists. B’s quote expires unused. Control never returns to `dispatch_allowed` after the resting observation, so a second order is not sent.

**P2. Same-domain queue, then execution.** The leg’s locus is the same-chain system contract. The payload commitment includes the CoreWriter action version. The EVM transaction is included and the log is enqueued (E5). Source is `included`, effect is `enqueued`, control is `dispatch_frozen`. EVM finality moves only the source rail to `final` (E6). The effect rail stays `enqueued`. A later core observation executes that action id (E7) and the effect rail becomes `full`. Derived outcome: `succeeded`. The enqueue receipt never satisfies a language transition that requires execution.

**P3. Partial destination delivery, then a residual refund.** Source burn of 100 becomes `final` (E5, E6) with the claim id inside `LegId`. Destination evidence delivers 40 and is final on the destination (E7, E6). Effect is `partial`, cumulative 40. A route proof states that this claim can deliver nothing more (E8). Refund of 60 is authorized and becomes `refund_final` on the source refund path (E6, E7). Accounting is 40 + 60 ≤ 100, fees included in the entitlement definition. Derived outcome: `closed_accounted`. The same claim id cannot mint again, by the route’s consumed nullifier or message nonce, which is the CCTP and ICS-004 pattern applied to this leg.

## Hostile traces

**H1. Late success after timeout.** Source is `final` for 100. The operational deadline passes. The kernel stores a timeout `ObservationId`. The effect rail is set to `unknown` if no destination fact exists, or left on its previous evidence if one does. No refund attempt is created. The Aeon probe rejected a full refund on `timed_out` with counterexample `sent=1, delivered=1`. Later, destination finality for 100 arrives (E7, E6). The effect rail moves from `unknown` to `full`. Derived outcome: `succeeded`. The timeout record stays in the log and does not reduce the cumulative. If a refund was sent anyway at the deadline and both the refund and the delivery reach finality, recovery becomes `breach`. The delivery is kept. Any makeup payment is a new compensation leg.

**H2. Partial destination delivery.** Source final amount is 100. Destination E7 shows 40. A second observer still reports observed delivery 0. A full refund of 100, whether justified by the zero observation, by status `unknown`, or by the partial itself, is refused. Those are three Aeon rejections, with counterexamples where actual delivery is already 1. The legal kernel state is cumulative 40, refund edge closed until E8 makes that cumulative exclusive, and then a refund of at most 60. An adapter that emits the refund of 100 anyway leaves both effects stored. Derived outcome: `breach`, because 40 + 100 exceeds 100.

**H3. Duplicated dispatch.** Attempt 1 is sent and the RPC session times out. Source for attempt 1 is `broadcast_unknown`. Control is `dispatch_frozen`. A faulty worker allocates attempt 2 under a fresh venue nonce and submits the same economic order again. Both attempts include. The venue now has two order ids, or the bridge has two claims, for one `LegId`. Reconciliation freezes the leg, records both cumulatives, and does not pick one as the real order. It does not refund “the” duplicate. Derived outcome: `breach` if the combined effects exceed the entitlement, otherwise `dispatch_frozen` with two open duties. The legal branch at the RPC timeout was to keep observing attempt 1. A new ordinal is available only after attempt 1 is `rejected_before_effect` or `dropped_before_final` by evidence, with the same payload commitment. ERC-4337’s nonce consumption is the analogous warning: seeing a nonce move, or failing to see a receipt, does not identify which payload the chain actually kept.

**H4. Signature, inclusion, or enqueue promoted to delivery.** The signer returns E3 for the authorized digest. A receipt writer marks the workflow delivered because a signature exists, because the source transaction is included, or because a CoreWriter log was emitted. The protocol leaves the effect rail at `none` or `enqueued`. A language rule that requires E7 does not fire. The Aeon signing probe, on its integer tags, rejected using the signed tag as broadcast, the signed tag as finalized, and the broadcast tag as finalized. The same probe accepted a `native` value declared finalized and named it `native` in the trust report. A host Boolean is that kind of premise. It is not E7. Separately, a sign request whose domain, path, digest, recipient, epoch, or nonce differs from `SignRequestId` is refused before the MPC or agent call. An adapter or key-epoch change after authorization invalidates the stored signature for broadcast. Consumed `SignRequestId`s remain stored after any external nonce prune. That is the direct consequence of Hyperliquid’s warning that a deregistered agent’s pruned nonce state can make old actions replayable if the address is reused.

**H5. Cancel races a fill, then a full refund is attempted.** Effect is `open_residual` with cumulative 0. A cancel attempt moves recovery to `cancel_requested`. Before the venue reports the order dead, a fill of 30 is imported (E7). The cancel then becomes effective for the remainder. Required state: delivered 30, residual dead, recovery `cancel_effective`. A refund of the original full quantity is `breach`. If cancel was requested while the source was still `broadcast_unknown` and no venue order id had been observed, recovery cannot enter `cancel_effective` at all. The unseen order may still fill. Herlihy’s admissible refund and ICS-004’s proof of non-receipt are the same constraint: the unfilled portion becomes refundable only after the venue or bridge establishes that this order or claim is dead at a stated cumulative.

## What the Aeon bridge experiment establishes

It establishes a narrow authoring result, and nothing about a live bridge.

The executed source was AeonLang 4.9.0 at commit `ef66bd95e6b7d2d5309453ee63640bc7fa1d988f`, Z3 5.1.0.0 and cvc5 1.4.0, driven with `strict_decidable=True`, synthesis budget 0, and no `native` escapes. Script SHA-256 `9fcacbad85a2a40c487ed99aa81512dd94f07e58aa3d2dfbd143979385ba0feb`. Raw judgment SHA-256 `df45213c73d6b8936c3b233d0fa53da2e02de142268e10aaff78e339be40bab4`. The predicate was `sent > 0`, `0 ≤ delivered ≤ sent`, `0 ≤ refund`, and `delivered + refund ≤ sent`, on mathematical integers.

Observed on that path:

| Policy | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Refund 0 while status is unknown | Accepted |
| Full refund on timeout alone | Rejected, counterexample `sent=1, delivered=1` |
| Full refund on unknown status | Rejected, same shape |
| Full refund when observed delivery is 0 | Rejected, because actual delivery can be 1 |
| Full refund after positive partial delivery | Rejected |
| Refund exactly `sent - delivered` | Accepted, with `delivered` supplied as a premise |
| Full refund under an input refinement `delivered = 0` | Accepted, because the checker trusts that refinement |

Status code 1 was an uninterpreted constant. `timed_out` had no semantic link to delivery. `observed_delivery` was allowed to lag actual delivery.

**Limits, in the experiment’s own terms.** No token scale, fee, representation ratio, supply, claim id, or foreign finality was modeled. The accepted residual refund is conditional on `delivered` already being complete and authoritative. If more destination credit can arrive after refund authorization, that arithmetic is not sufficient. The probe does not show replay protection, adapter byte correspondence, or a Moriarty or Midnight judgment. No transaction was submitted.

**A further limit from the same packet.** The authority experiment on the same pin accepted `v = 101 && v <= 100` and a bare `false` term, with fresh-process exit code 0, while a split cap obligation was rejected. The bridge rejections are real observations about those terms. They are not a soundness certificate for Aeon as an admission, refund, or settlement gate. A repaired checker would still only discharge arithmetic after some other component justifies `delivered`. The signing experiment’s `native` finalized token is the same class of limit: a type-level phase tag can catch a confused phase in a checked source, and a host annotation can satisfy the checker without a ledger.

Use of Aeon that matches the evidence: an offline probe of a conservation formula once premises are explicit. The kernel and the settlement verifier still have to establish the premises, the claim identity, the exclusivity certificate, and the late-delivery race.

## How the pieces fit the language

The kernel may implement `quote → validatePlan → reserve → authorize → dispatch → observe → reconcile → advanceOrRecover` as procedure names. Each name appends facts on Design B. `advanceOrRecover` is the pure derivation plus, when the guards hold, one new authorized leg for cancel, refund, or compensation.

The intent language accepts a transition when the imported observations satisfy the signed evidence profile for that locus. It does not read the kernel’s control rail. Service refusal, solver downtime, or a frozen `unknown` leg leaves a direct Midnight program’s validity unchanged.

Application profiles (AMM, loan, vault, perp, and the others) call this protocol. They do not each grow a private retry machine. A bridge profile adds claim, representation ratio, cumulative destination delivery, refund exclusion, and the bridge’s own trust policy on top of the same ids and rails.

## Open decisions

These remain owner choices. This memo does not infer them from NEAR or Hyperliquid.

1. Canonical hash and exact bytes for the identifiers. M4-C5.
2. Custody model, and who can move bridge keys and signing keys.
3. Whether each foreign fact is an in-circuit proof or a named quorum, and which destination contracts are only signature-enforcing.
4. The first external adapter, and whether that venue enforces a client idempotency key. Without one, Design B’s freeze rule still applies, and automatic retry is unavailable for any send that reaches `broadcast_unknown`.
5. The finality policy admitted on that first adapter.
6. Whether that profile allows partial fills or requires fill-or-kill. Design B can represent either. The envelope has to pick one.
7. The exclusivity evidence for the first bridge: consumed message nonce, nullifier, or an explicit remainder statement, and which issuer may sign it.
8. How long `unknown` may persist before a person is asked to look, and who may escalate. The escalation record is not E8.
9. Key-epoch retirement while an attempt is `broadcast_unknown` or `included`.
10. Whether recovery spending authority lives in the user envelope or in a separate named grant, and who funds compensation.
11. Solver bonding and service fees, after this safety contract is fixed.
12. Whether any authoring checker, including a later Aeon, is allowed to gate U5. The recommendation here is no: U5 acceptance is exact-byte adapter fixtures, observed effects, and the hostile traces above.
